item.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon jury hears Triple Zero call from day of alleged murders
item.description: A jury has been played a Triple Zero (000) call from the phone of Luke Davies on the morning he and his boyfriend, Jesse Baird, were allegedly murdered by then-police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon.

media:group.media:description: Beau Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder.

item.title: Rogue OpenAI agent accessed second NSW government website
item.description: The rogue AI agent entered a National Parks and Wildlife Service web application containing publicly available historical information and data on fires.

media:group.media:description: OpenAI has confirmed another incident affecting a NSW government website, with no personal data breached.

item.title: Former Liberal politician Bruce Baird dies aged 84
item.description: The party stalwart was father to former NSW premier Mike Baird and journalist Julia Baird.

media:group.media:description: Former Liberal MP Bruce Baird has died.

item.title: The stolen Ukrainian teen who became the poster boy for Putin's propaganda
item.description: Russia is not just abducting Ukrainian kids, it is embarking on a campaign of mass indoctrination, as Denys Kostev experienced firsthand.

media:group.media:description: Denys in the red beret of Russia's "Young Army" cadets.

item.title: Notorious alleged WA drug kingpin 'The Kid' arrested in Colombia
item.description: Australian-Iranian national Arash Ebrahimi Far is arrested in Colombia while leaving hospital after being "wounded by gunfire".

media:group.media:description: Arash Ebrahimi Far has been arrested by the National Police of Colombia.

item.title: 'I was fighting for my life': flydubai pilot recounts harrowing mid-flight attack
item.description: Captain Smit Machchhar has been hailed a hero for his actions aboard a flydubai flight after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane began a steep descent.

media:group.media:description: Smit Machchhar talks with Narendra Modi from hospital.

item.title: 'Very violent' home invasions targeted women alone, police say
item.description: Three men have been charged over violent home invasions, as police investigate whether the group were planning to target a third victim.

media:group.media:description: Superintendent Virginia Gorman condemned the "excessive violence" used in home invasions that allegedly targeted women home alone.

item.title: Commonwealth Bank boss says Reserve Bank rate hikes probably finished
item.description: While the bank believes the RBA is done it all hangs on the next lot of inflation data released late this month, Mr Comyn said, as he talked productivity, AI and housing with the ABC's Alan Kohler.
item.dc:creator: Alison Branley

media:group.media:description: Chief Executive of Commonwealth Bank, Matt Comyn spoke with the ABC's Alan Kohler.

item.title: 'Lifeless' baby took two gasps after delivery, inquest hears
item.description: One expert has told the court there were likely signs of life when Alby Spreadborough was born at Emerald Hospital, while another disagreed.
item.dc:creator: Emily Anderson

media:group.media:description: Rebecca and Tim Spreadborough with a photo of Alby, who weighed 3.3 kilograms when he was born.

item.title: Healthcare workers killed in Ledcourt triple-fatal had a 'bright' future in Australia
item.description: Regional Victorian couple who died in a multi-vehicle crash are remembered as "loving" and "caring" people.

item.title: Perth man accused of letting toddler steer car appears in court
item.description: Jake Douglas Smith is alleged to have uploaded a video to social media showing a small child steering a car through a residential area.

media:group.media:description: The video uploaded to social media appeared to show a small child steering a car.

item.title: Roosters blow as Watson ruled out of NRL grand final
item.description: Roosters hooker Connor Watson will miss the NRL grand final after failing to get clearance to play following a concussion suffered in the preliminary final victory against the Dolphins.

media:group.media:description: Connor Watson suffered a head knock against the Dolphins.

item.title: Amy Shark to lead NRL grand final musical tribute to Jai Arrow

media:group.media:description: Amy Shark is set to provide NRL grand final musical entertainment alongside a supergroup of Aussie musicians.

item.title: NRLW grand final marks end of era
item.description: One year on from the greatest and most controversial grand final in NRLW history, the Roosters and Broncos meet again for a showdown that marks a turning point for the most dominant side of recent years.

media:group.media:description: Millie Elliott will lead the Roosters forwards one last time in the NRLW grand final.

item.title: Christa Pike fighting for life after surviving execution attempt
item.description: After 30 years on death row, the teenage killer was set to become the first woman executed in the US state of Tennessee in more than 200 years.

media:group.media:description: Christa Pike was sentenced to death for the murder of Colleen Slemmer, a crime committed when she was 18 years old.

item.title: Minister's Trump lamb plan labelled 'ill-informed' by super sector
item.description: Trade Minister Don Farrell asks the Trump administration to consider sparing Australian sheep farmers from future tariffs in exchange for Australian investment in America's lamb industry.
item.dc:creator: Brad Ryan

media:group.media:description: The US is one of Australia's most valuable overseas markets for lamb as the meat's popularity grows.

item.title: Bookkeeper admits defrauding $2.8m from farming family
item.description: Michelle Kathleen Lawson discussed the hardships of farming with the family that employed her for almost two decades while secretly taking from their accounts, a court has heard.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Testa

media:group.media:description: Michelle Kathleen Lawson, 53, defrauded the farming family that employed her in Tully, between Cairns and Townsville.

item.title: Inquiry hears 'blue code of silence' stops DV victims reporting police
item.description: Victim-survivors of police officers are concerned they will not be believed or treated seriously because of the "interconnected relationships" that police have with each other, a Tasmanian inquiry hears.
item.dc:creator: Scout Wallen

media:group.media:description: The inquiry heard there was a perceived culture of police banding together to protect their own.

item.title: Woman who stopped Adelaide beach brawl speaks out
item.description: In an exclusive interview with the ABC, a woman who tried to stop a brawl on an Adelaide beach before being pelted with bottles has spoken publicly for the first time.
item.dc:creator: Will Hunter and Sophie Landau

media:group.media:description: Kate intervenes in a fight at Glenelg on Tuesday.

item.title: Bluebottles the size of a fist wash up on Gold Coast beaches
item.description: Unusually large bluebottles are washing ashore on the Gold Coast ahead of summer, with scientists unsure how their venom compares with that of smaller species.

media:group.media:description: A large bluebottle that washed ashore on the Gold Coast.

item.title: Tasmania's top prosecutor rules out 'further action' on town hall snack saga
item.description: Tasmania's top prosecutor has declined to take action over the taking of snacks from Hobart Town Hall by the city's deputy lord mayor, potentially bringing the contentious saga to a close.

media:group.media:description: Zelinda Sherlock was captured on CCTV taking snacks and drinks from an elected member's lounge in Hobart Town Hall, alongside an unidentified person.

item.title: Which states get a public holiday on Monday?
item.description: Many Australians will enjoy a long weekend this weekend, but half the country will miss out on a public holiday.

item.title: How Assefa ran third fastest marathon ever despite 'destroyed' Achilles
item.description: Tigst Assefa ran the final two kilometres of the Berlin Marathon with a badly damaged Achilles tendon, which required immediate surgery to repair. She still ran the third-fastest women's marathon in history.
item.dc:creator: Simon Smale

media:group.media:description: Tigst Assefa was in agony for the last few kilometres of the race.
